name: Ethbaal
overview: Ethbaal was a male king of the Sidonians and is notably identified as the father of Jezebel. His rule and family connections are briefly mentioned in the biblical text without further tribal or familial details. He is recognized primarily for his political and familial role in the context of Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Ethbaal means 'with [him is] Baal,' indicating a connection to the Canaanite deity Baal, reflecting the religious context of his time. He also held the title 'king of the Sidonians,' which identifies his political authority over the Sidonian people as recorded in 1 Kings 16:31.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ethbaal as the father of Jezebel, linking him directly to a significant biblical figure. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ethbaal's significance lies in his role as the father of Jezebel, who plays a pivotal role in the narrative of Israel's kings. His kingship over the Sidonians situates him as a foreign ruler whose family connections influenced Israel's religious and political challenges. His mention in 1 Kings 16:31 highlights the intersection of foreign influence and idolatry in Israel's history.
